clue.text: I don't believe this solver's MO!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, an Irish-flavoured 'get away'
second meaning, read literally: a method (a way) that belongs to the person solving, addressed as 'you'

explanation.walkthrough: Split the phrase as A WAY WITH YOU: MO is modus operandi, a way of working, and the setter addresses the solver as 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a common exclamation meaning 'nonsense, pull the other one', said when someone tells you something hard to credit.

clue.text: Overcooked congratulations?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: steak cooked all the way through, which many would call overdone
second meaning: the phrase you say to praise an achievement

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a steak cooked this way is only overcooked in some diners' opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes meat cooked thoroughly with no pink left, and is also the everyday exclamation of praise for success.

clue.text: See 26
Implicating publication left by cop with a constituent

indicators.note: to implicate originally meant to fold or twist together, so the letters get entangled into a new order
whatever has been left by something has had that thing go away from it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these three letters go
taken as written; this letter goes too

explanation.surface: A news story implicates a policeman and someone he represents.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike C, O, P and A out of PUBLICATION and the remaining seven letters rearrange to IN-BUILT. 'Implicating' sounds like accusing; here it means intertwining.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forming an integral part of a whole is a constituent part of it, built in from the start rather than added later.

clue.text: Delay part of costume rental for Spooner's Dracula?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so his version of a phrase has its initial sounds exchanged

parts.note: a vampire costume needs fake fangs; swap the opening sound with the next word
hire is rental; its opening sound trades places with the first word's
surface padding that tells you whose costume, pointing the first piece at a vampire's teeth

explanation.surface: A fancy-dress shop rents out a vampire's fake teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Dracula is only there to point at fangs: FANG HIRE, said with its first sounds swapped, becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang fire is an idiom from old guns slow to discharge, meaning to hold back or postpone acting.

clue.text: The head holds obtrusively religious view

indicators.note: something that holds another thing keeps it inside itself

parts.note: onion is old British slang for the head, as in 'off your onion'
pi is crossword shorthand for pious, sanctimoniously devout

explanation.surface: A religious leader parades their devoutness and holds a firm outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The head' looks like a church or school leader, but it is slang for the skull: 'off one's onion' means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a personal belief or judgment about something, which is exactly what an opinion amounts to.

clue.text: Responding to call for attention, secure building properly?

parts.note: to secure a door is to bolt it
a building put up right, standing straight and level

explanation.surface: A builder answers a call to make the structure safe and sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secure building properly' reads as one instruction about construction; split it as a fastening word plus a description of a well-made structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone snapping to attention, like a soldier, stands or sits perfectly straight, rigidly erect with spine stiff.

clue.text: Influenced by space invader entering former washroom?

indicators.note: whatever is entering something ends up inside it

parts.note: the late chairman is the former one
under the influence of
E.T., Spielberg's extra-terrestrial visitor

explanation.surface: An alien has moved into an old bathroom and is affecting things.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two pieces join and sit inside LATE. 'Washroom' usually means a toilet; the question mark flags the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A launderette is a self-service laundry, a public room full of machines where people wash clothes, hence a wash room.

clue.text: Daughter's face when leaving old man animated is a picture

indicators.note: animated means set moving and lively, so the letters move about into a new order
something leaving goes away, so it is taken out

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a face is the front of something, so only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: its first letter, which also abbreviates daughter, is removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl's expression lights up when her elderly father perks up, a sight worth seeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is a picture' is an idiom for a delightful face, but 'is a' is wordplay and 'picture' alone is the definition. Fittingly, the painting is famous for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait in the Louvre is perhaps the best-known painting in the world, so it is a picture by example.

clue.text: Large church seizes a note to Italian group

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab hold of it and keep it within your grasp

parts.note: Church of England
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
taken as written
nota bene, the abbreviation used to flag a note
'to' as in 'add to', meaning plus
IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A cathedral grabs a score for an Italian ensemble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large church' looks like one idea, but the size word goes inside the church abbreviation. The clue reads as if 'Italian group' is the band; the group is British, and 'Italian' is just IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean Bandit is a British electronic and classical crossover band, known for 'Rather Be', so a musical group by example.

clue.text: See 24
Starter pack on all alloys containing erbium

indicators.note: something containing another has it inside before anything else happens
to alloy is to melt metals together, so the letters are fused and recast in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Er is the chemical symbol for erbium

explanation.surface: A beginner's kit for metalworkers, every alloy including a rare-earth element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter pack' reads as one phrase, a beginner's kit, but the definition stops at 'Starter' and the next words go into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A pancake roll is the British name for a spring roll, typically served as a first course in Chinese restaurants.

clue.text: Village idiot is smashing alternative to Perspex butt

indicators.note: something smashing through a pane ends up in the middle of it

parts.note: Perspex is a clear plastic used instead of panes of the traditional material
a gowk is a Scottish and northern dialect word for a fool
taken as written

explanation.surface: The local fool is breaking windows, a mess plastic sheeting would have avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' fits the surface image of breaking a pane, but it only places the idiot inside. 'Butt' is the verb-turned-noun, a blow with the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A Glasgow kiss is British slang for a headbutt, a blow struck with the forehead, ironically named after the Scottish city.

clue.text: Including everyone in alert, Queen's intro to Lady Gaga?

indicators.note: one thing turning to another means it changes into it, so one letter group is swapped out

parts.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's royal cipher, is the part swapped out

indicators.note: an intro is the opening, so just the beginning letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter replaces the royal cipher
gaga means senile, which suggests aged

explanation.surface: A warning goes out to everyone that Queen are introducing Lady Gaga, who took her name from their song Radio Ga Ga.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks like the rock band whose song gave Lady Gaga her name, and the italics suggest a title; here it is the late Queen's royal cipher, and gaga simply means senile.
explanation.definitionFit: All told is an idiom meaning in total, when every item or person has been counted and added together.

clue.text: Capital "acquired" by elevating son of nobleman …

indicators.note: whatever is acquired by someone ends up held within their possession
in a down entry, elevating something lifts it so it runs upward, bottom to top

parts.note: a son is a boy or lad
UC is the printer's abbreviation for upper case, a capital letter

explanation.surface: A nobleman's son raises funds, acquiring capital for the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money or a city but is the printing term for a capital letter. The quotation marks warn that 'acquired' is working as a device, and the ellipsis runs on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducal is the adjective for a duke, the highest rank of British peer, so it means belonging to such a nobleman.

clue.text: Cockney shouldn't credit 26 3 Down's forgotten snack

indicators.note: what is forgotten has dropped out of mind, so it is left out

parts.note: a porky pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie, something not to be believed
the solution to 26 and 3 Down is 'this year', and Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A Londoner can't believe the current year's snack has been forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang replaces a word with a phrase that rhymes with it: porky pie for lie, often cut to 'porky'. Lose the year's abbreviation from it to reach the British snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A pork pie is a British cold savoury pastry filled with chopped pork, commonly eaten as a picnic or pub snack.

clue.text: … Crown reported offence

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: the crown of a hill is its summit

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the previous clue's nobleman, making the crown look royal; it is the top of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is resentment from wounded pride, the feeling of someone who takes offence at a slight.

clue.text: Course regularly followed around home city

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the opposite way, so the piece runs backwards

parts.note: a rut is a fixed, monotonous routine
at home means in

explanation.surface: A route is routinely taken round someone's home town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' tempts you to take alternate letters of 'Course', but it belongs to the description of a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in north-west Italy, capital of Piedmont, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Make random selection, as does recruiter of extras for crowd scenes?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: decide by drawing straws or tokens

definitions.text: as does recruiter of extras for crowd scenes
definitions.note: describes the action rather than naming it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a director hiring many extras at once, choosing performers for roles in bulk

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: a film's casting agent casts lots of people for a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting lots is the ancient practice of choosing by chance, throwing marked objects to decide an outcome impartially.

clue.text: See 5
Retired Communist probed by British maybe packing on board

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the whole piece runs backwards
a probe pokes inside something, so the prober ends up within

parts.note: Mao Zedong, the Chinese Communist leader
a British person is from the UK; 'maybe' signals an example

explanation.surface: An old Communist is investigated by British intelligence, perhaps while travelling by ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first and the whole combination is then turned round. 'On board' sounds like a passenger, but it places the packing on a ship's planks.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose tarred hemp fibre that sailors hammered into the seams of wooden ships to make them watertight.

clue.text: In one's first article naughtily imply Games were held here

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it
behaving naughtily means misbehaving, so the letters will not stay in line
first means the opening position, so only the starting letter is used

parts.note: its first letter
taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone's debut piece of writing slyly hints at where some contest took place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First article' looks like a debut piece of writing, but 'first' belongs to 'one's' and 'article' is just A.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia in ancient Greece was the sanctuary of Zeus where the original Olympic athletic contests were staged every four years.

clue.text: Mate of a man in green keeps this chap out of the Green Man

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

parts.words: Mate of a man in green
parts.note: Maid Marian, sweetheart of Robin Hood, who dressed in Lincoln green

indicators.note: taking one thing out of another means removing it

parts.note: taken as written
the pronoun for a male, removed from the word before it

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's sweetheart bars a fellow from the local pub called the Green Man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Green Man is a common English pub name and a pagan figure, but here the definition means the little green men of science fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens from Mars are traditionally pictured as little green men, so a green man is a playful description of a Martian.

clue.text: Wise guy repealing criminal law on knife cases

indicators.note: repealing means revoking or undoing, so the letters run in the opposite direction
a case encloses its contents, so the wanted letters are tucked inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: A smart alec argues for scrapping the law against carrying knives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' and 'knife' suggest an anagram of law plus a blade; instead the answer runs backwards through those words.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise guy is a smart alec who acts as though he has all the answers, the same idea as one claiming total knowledge.

clue.text: Range being talked about?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the distance within which a voice can be heard

definitions.note: a state rather than a noun, read as a phrase
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split as two words: the burning feeling said to come when others gossip about you

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as EARS HOT: folklore says your ears burn when someone is talking about you.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the range of hearing, the distance within which spoken words or sounds can be caught by a listener.

clue.text: Clean up after flying kite during bad weather

indicators.note: something happening during another event sits within its span

parts.note: rain as an example of bad weather

indicators.note: something flying is tossed about in the air, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tidying the garden after a kite-flying session spoilt by a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clean up after' reads as tidying a mess; here 'clean up' means to make a killing and 'after' just joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up is an idiom for making a large profit, and raking money in describes earning lots of it quickly.

clue.text: See 18
One form hysteria may take nowadays

indicators.note: a form is a shape something can be moulded into, so the letters are rearranged
the form something may take is one of its possible rearrangements

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A comment on the shape modern panic tends to take.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as social commentary, but 'form' tells you to reshape the eight letters of the condition into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Within the current twelve months is a loose way of saying at the present time, the sense of the adverb nowadays.

clue.text: See 2
Excited about delivery of welcome money

parts.note: what someone is about is what they are up to

indicators.note: a speaker's delivery is the way words are spoken, so their sound is what matters

parts.note: hi is a greeting and dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled about a delivery of much-needed cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' sounds like a parcel of money arriving; it means speaking. 'About' looks like a container signal but is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to high doh is a Scottish idiom for being in a frantic, overwrought state of excitement or agitation.

clue.text: See 9
More than one bulk SMS interpreted by cruciverbalists?

indicators.note: setters describe letter strings in words, so the arrangement of the letters is put into a setter's phrasing

parts.note: read as a setter would describe it: the middle letter M, abbreviation for mass, sits in two S letters, all spelt out in words

explanation.surface: A crossword buff decodes a mass text message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulk SMS' suggests mass texting; instead describe SMS as a setter would: M is in SS, which spelt out gives mass in esses.
explanation.definitionFit: Massiness is the quality of being bulky or weighty, so its plural form covers more than one such bulk.
